signature: SUBROUTINE DLAQR0( WANTT, WANTZ, N, ILO, IHI, H, LDH, WR, WI,

returns.workDependent: the QR iteration's path depends on LWORK, as the reference's does; with 1 or 2 elements it makes no progress and returns INFO = IHI, as the compiled reference does

params.name: wantt
params.reference: = .TRUE. : the full Schur form T is required; = .FALSE.: only eigenvalues are required.

params.name: wantz
params.reference: = .TRUE. : the matrix of Schur vectors Z is required; = .FALSE.: Schur vectors are not required.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix H. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: ihi
params.reference: It is assumed that H is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N and, if $\mathrm{ILO} > 1$, `H(ILO,ILO-1)` is zero. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to DGEBAL, and then passed to DGEHRD when the matrix output by DGEBAL is reduced to Hessenberg form. Otherwise, `ILO` and `IHI` should be set to 1 and N, respectively. If $N > 0$, then $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$. If $N = 0$, then `ILO = 1` and `IHI = 0`.

params.name: H
params.reference:
On entry, the upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if `INFO = 0` and `WANTT` is .TRUE., then H contains the upper quasi-triangular matrix T from the Schur decomposition (the Schur form); 2-by-2 diagonal blocks (corresponding to complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues) are returned in standard form, with $H(i,i) = H(i+1,i+1)$ and $H(i+1,i) \, H(i,i+1) < 0$. If `INFO = 0` and `WANTT` is .FALSE., then the contents of H are unspecified on exit. (The output value of H when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)

This subroutine may explicitly set $H(i,j) = 0$ for $i > j$ and $j = 1$, 2, ... `ILO`-1 or $j = \mathrm{IHI}+1$, `IHI`+2, ... N.
params.workDependent: the QR iteration's path depends on LWORK (AED window <= LWORK/2, shifts <= 2*LWORK/3), as the reference's does; with 1 or 2 elements it makes no progress (INFO > 0)

params.name: ldh
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array H. $\mathrm{LDH} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: WR
params.workDependent: the QR iteration's path depends on LWORK (AED window <= LWORK/2, shifts <= 2*LWORK/3), as the reference's does; with 1 or 2 elements it makes no progress (INFO > 0)

params.name: WI
params.reference: The real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues of `H(ILO:IHI,ILO:IHI)` are stored in `WR(ILO:IHI)` and `WI(ILO:IHI)`. If two eigenvalues are computed as a complex conjugate pair, they are stored in consecutive elements of `WR` and `WI`, say the i-th and (i+1)th, with $\mathrm{WI}(i) > 0$ and $\mathrm{WI}(i+1) < 0$. If `WANTT` is .TRUE., then the eigenvalues are stored in the same order as on the diagonal of the Schur form returned in H, with `WR(i) = H(i,i)` and, if `H(i:i+1,i:i+1)` is a 2-by-2 diagonal block, `WI(i) = sqrt(-H(i+1,i)*H(i,i+1))` and `WI(i+1) = -WI(i)`.
params.workDependent: the QR iteration's path depends on LWORK (AED window <= LWORK/2, shifts <= 2*LWORK/3), as the reference's does; with 1 or 2 elements it makes no progress (INFO > 0)

params.name: ihiz
params.reference: Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.. $1 \le \mathrm{ILOZ} \le \mathrm{ILO}$; $\mathrm{IHI} \le \mathrm{IHIZ} \le N$.

params.name: Z
params.reference: If `WANTZ` is .FALSE., then Z is not referenced. If `WANTZ` is .TRUE., then `Z(ILO:IHI,ILOZ:IHIZ)` is replaced by $Z(\mathrm{ILO}:\mathrm{IHI},\mathrm{ILOZ}:\mathrm{IHIZ}) \, U$ where U is the orthogonal Schur factor of `H(ILO:IHI,ILO:IHI)`. (The output value of Z when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)
params.workDependent: the QR iteration's path depends on LWORK (AED window <= LWORK/2, shifts <= 2*LWORK/3), as the reference's does; with 1 or 2 elements it makes no progress (INFO > 0)

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Z. if `WANTZ` is .TRUE. then $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge \max (1,\mathrm{IHIZ})$. Otherwise, $\mathrm{LDZ} \ge 1$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `LWORK = -1`, `WORK(1)` returns an estimate of the optimal value for `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,N)$ is sufficient, but `LWORK` typically as large as $6 \, N$ may be required for optimal performance. A workspace query to determine the optimal workspace size is recommended.

If `LWORK = -1`, then DLAQR0 does a workspace query. In this case, DLAQR0 checks the input parameters and estimates the optimal workspace size for the given values of N, `ILO` and `IHI`. The estimate is returned in `WORK(1)`. No error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA. Neither H nor Z are accessed.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, DLAQR0 failed to compute all of the eigenvalues.  Elements 1:ilo-1 and i+1:n of `WR` and `WI` contain those eigenvalues which have been successfully computed.  (Failures are rare.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and WANT is .FALSE., then on exit, the remaining unconverged eigenvalues are the eigen- values of the upper Hessenberg matrix rows and columns `ILO` through `INFO` of the final, output value of H.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `WANTT` is .TRUE., then on exit

```text
(*)  (initial value of H)*U  = U*(final value of H)
```

where U is an orthogonal matrix. The final value of H is upper Hessenberg and quasi-triangular in rows and columns `INFO`+1 through `IHI`.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `WANTZ` is .TRUE., then on exit

(final value of `Z(ILO:IHI,ILOZ:IHIZ)` = (initial value of $Z(\mathrm{ILO}:\mathrm{IHI},\mathrm{ILOZ}:\mathrm{IHIZ}) \, U$

where U is the orthogonal matrix in (\*) (regard- less of the value of `WANTT`.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `WANTZ` is .FALSE., then Z is not accessed.

overrides.reason: DLAQR0 caps its aggressive-early-deflation window at NW <= LWORK/2 and its simultaneous shifts at NS <= 2*LWORK/3, and DLAQR3 and DLAQR5 then pick their block sizes from the WORK they are given, so the reference's own QR iteration depends on LWORK: below its documented max(1,N) (which it neither checks nor needs) it is accepted but takes another path, and at LWORK = 1 or 2 (no window, no shifts) it makes no progress and returns INFO = IHI with H and Z partly reduced. Compiled LAPACK 3.12.0 does this too: N = 140 and 300 (random Hessenberg and the cyclic shift) at LWORK = 1, 2 return INFO = N, at LWORK = 3 INFO = 139/284/300, at LWORK >= 4 INFO = 0, never writing past WORK(LWORK). The Schur form and vectors are unique only up to the order and signs the path picks. The module's tests check LWORK = 1 (INFO = N, as the reference) and a few elements past the blocking threshold (all eigenvalues found) (ticket 0016).
